claim: Human retrieval order is literal similarity ~ surface similarity >> analogy > first-order-only (proportion reminded .56, .53, .12, .09; 32 stories, 20 probes, about a week delay), while soundness ratings run the other way for surface matches.
agent_test: Build a memory of past solved items; probe with new items that are surface-similar vs structure-only; measure what the agent retrieves versus what it rates as useful, at fixed token budget.

claim: Surface dominance is conditional: with cues combining surface and structure, close analogues beat distant ones (0.47 vs 0.09 per person, N=133), but when familiar structures meet unusual surfaces, distant analogues beat surface matches (0.46 vs 0.04, N=81; video clips 71.7% structure vs 18.6% surface).
agent_test: Test agent retrieval with cues whose structure is a familiar named pattern vs an unfamiliar one; expect structural retrieval to rise with familiar pattern labels.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Two-stage retrieval (cheap content-vector filter, then structural match on survivors) reproduces the human order in simulation and is about 100x faster than the ARCS constraint-network rival, which gets the order wrong and is swamped by larger memory.
agent_test: Compare one-shot embedding top-k vs cheap filter + LLM structural rerank on a fixed memory at equal tokens. Single-source because all numbers come from one lab's simulations on tiny memories. Gap search 2026-11-01: still no published head-to-head of cheap filter + LLM rerank vs one-stage top-k vs stuffing at equal tokens on analogue retrieval. Nearest: CPR (d06) shows rerank works and costs about 20 calls; Self-Route (d08) shows retrieve-then-escape-hatch reaches stuffing accuracy at 38-61 percent of tokens on knowledge QA.

claim: The MAC/FAC fit depends on narrow selector widths (MAC 10-20 percent, FAC at least 10 percent) and on content vectors that mix attributes and relations; attribute-only or relation-only vectors fail.
agent_test: Sweep the shortlist size in the filter stage; look for a band where analogies surface without junk.

claim: Comparing two analogous cases at recall time makes people retrieve structurally matching cases from memory (retrieval rating 1.25 vs 0.82, N=124; Exp 2 replication 1.47 vs 0.59, N=36; Exp 4 analogue recalled 27% vs 6%, N=73).
agent_test: Before retrieving, have the agent compare two current problems (or restate a problem as an abstract schema) and see whether structure-level retrieval improves. Same authors for every experiment, but replicated across samples.

claim: The comparison benefit does not reliably carry to problem solving: tumor problem 31% vs 5% (N=227), but the second problem 41% vs 30% was not significant, and explicit reminding was equally rare (18% vs 14%).
agent_test: Check solution gain from a compare-then-solve prompt on two problem families.

claim: Storing abstracted relational schemas in memory lets MAC/FAC retrieve analogues far more than raw cases do; adding literal items crowds both out (simulations only, 76 stories). LLM-agent follow-up (gap 2, partly closed): distilled or abstracted entries beat raw retrieved cases on agent benchmarks (see K26), but no study measures structural retrieval rate for schema vs raw trace.
agent_test: Write a compact schema note after each solved item and retrieve on those instead of raw traces; compare cross-domain retrieval.

claim: Hints turn analogy use on: classic Gick-Holyoak results are about 30% unhinted vs 80-90% hinted; a 2025 business replication found lower rates (6.3% and 20.3% unhinted; 8.7% and 37% hinted).
agent_test: Compare no-hint vs a 'consider analogous past problems' instruction on the agent at equal tokens.

claim: GPT-4 shows the reverse profile to humans: with no hint it never used the correct source story (0 of 60 runs); with a hint it flagged the right story every time but also the wrong one (precision about 0.5).
agent_test: Run the Gick-Holyoak design on the agent; require the agent to verify the mapping before use.

claim: LLMs and sentence embeddings are surface-bound on analogy: near analogies well recognised (about 75%), far analogies at or below chance (about 34-45%), humans over 91%.
agent_test: Measure agent retrieval on near vs far analogy sets (ARN, StoryAnalogy); a plain cosine embedding baseline should fail far cases.

claim: Long-context LLMs are near random at retrieving analogous stories from a bank, except GPT-4 Turbo on one-sentence stories (P@3 42.9% at 1 sentence, 3.9% at 30 sentences); the gap to humans grows with length.
agent_test: Use AnaloBench T2 as a retrieval probe; compare stuffing the bank in context with a two-stage filter.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Reasoning-intensive and cross-field retrieval is far below ordinary retrieval for off-the-shelf embedders: BRIGHT nDCG@10 18.3 vs MTEB 59.0; CPR-eval Recall@10 0.26 for the best retriever vs 0.07 chance.
agent_test: Rerank embedder top-k with the LLM itself; measure recall at equal token cost.

claim: Using an LLM as reranker or query rewriter over a shortlist recovers most of the lost structure: CPR-eval LLM reranker 0.81 vs best retriever 0.26 (151 candidates, 20.2 calls and $0.071 per query); BRIGHT reasoning-trace queries up to +12.2 nDCG@10, GPT-4 rerank of top-10 +3.1 over BM25 and no gain from widening to 100 (17.4 vs 17.0).
agent_test: Test 'LLM rewrites the problem into abstract form, then retrieve' against raw-query retrieval.

claim: Fine-tuning a retriever on cross-topic pairs lifts recall strongly (0.12 to 0.50, 0.17 to 0.69, 0.25 to 0.70) and transfers to held-out fields; training on web search or citation data does not.
agent_test: Not testable on a scaffold-only agent; shows the gap is a training-signal problem, so a scaffold must supply the structure.

claim: Retrievers or selectors aimed at usefulness or structure coverage beat pure similarity for in-context examples (EPR +6 to +7 EM; diverse coverage up to +23 points; RA-RFT 47.4 vs GRPO 43.3).
agent_test: Select examples by coverage of needed sub-structures rather than top-k similarity.

claim: Whether retrieving whole-task experience at the start hurts depends on the setting. HippoSpark: GPT-5.4-mini vanilla .326 vs Trajectory Experience .255, and bottleneck-triggered retrieval .483 (but .409 of that comes before any experience is added). RA-RFT: off-the-shelf embedding retrieval (38.5) is no better than a random trace (37.6) and below GRPO without retrieval (43.3), and untrained models start lower with retrieved traces. ExpeL: task-level retrieval at the start helped (ALFWorld 59.0 vs ReAct 40.0) and step-level re-retrieval was worse (48.5).
agent_test: Compare retrieve-at-start vs retrieve-at-stuck-point vs both, at equal tokens, with the same retrieval key. Differences between papers come from the key (task text vs stuck-state description), the benchmark and the model.

claim: Self-generated analogous problems beat zero-shot CoT by 2.0 to 10.7 points on GSM8K (GPT-3.5 77.8 vs 75.8; PaLM2 81.7 vs 78.2) and 3.4 to 5.0 on MATH, and beat fixed 5-shot CoT by 0.5 to 7.0. Versus retrieved exemplars (GSM8K, SBERT top-5) they lose for small models and win only for the largest: curie 2 vs 3, davinci-001 9 vs 11, davinci-002 48 vs 47, davinci-003 61 vs 57. On Codeforces the exemplar-only gain over 3-shot CoT is +2 Acc@1 for GPT-3.5 and 0 for GPT-4.
agent_test: Table 1 row labels are settled (d01): 75.0 is the 0-shot GPT-3.5 row. Untested for current frontier models; the DeepSeek-R1 note (d04) says few-shot hurts that reasoning model.

claim: Retrieving past successful trajectories by task similarity helps agents (ExpeL ALFWorld 59.0% vs ReAct 40.0%, random trajectories 42.5%); reason-similarity retrieval gave 48.5%. Insights-only vs retrieve-only: HotpotQA 36 vs 31, ALFWorld 50 vs 55, WebShop 37 vs 38.
agent_test: Replicate with task-similarity vs structure-similarity keys.

claim: Structure-labelled indexes (purpose and mechanism) beat text embeddings for analogy search and ideation (precision at top 1% 0.739 vs TF-IDF 0.630; good ideas 46% vs 37% random vs 30% TF-IDF).
agent_test: Index memory items by (purpose, mechanism) summaries written by the agent; compare with a raw-text index.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human-provided analogy guidance can unlock cross-domain solutions (Stokes law used 0/20 baseline vs 18/20; success 10% vs 100%), but this tests a hint, not retrieval.
agent_test: Treat as support for the hint effect only; a retrieval version needs automatic selection.

claim: LLM analogy ability is fragile under counterfactual or unfamiliar alphabets, and a 2024 study partly fails to replicate Webb et al. 2023 (humans .753 vs GPT-3 .488, GPT-4 .452).
agent_test: Check analogy retrieval with unfamiliar-surface tests, not familiar benchmarks.

claim: Deep-research agents rarely use structural analogies (0 of 22 past, 0 of 20 forward hidden-factor items); structural decomposition before retrieval helps, but its margin over self-reflection is small for stronger models (sonnet-4-6 4.11 vs 4.17).
agent_test: Compare decompose-then-retrieve vs reflect-then-retrieve at equal tokens.

claim: Analogies are rare in ordinary text (about 3% of a scientific corpus); SBERT top-100 precision is 100% only because it finds mostly self analogies, while structural mining reaches 72-79%.
agent_test: Do not assume an analogue exists in memory; log how often a structural analogue exists before testing retrieval.

claim: Case-based retrieval with fine-tuned embeddings gave only a small gain (+1.94% semantic similarity).
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Experts and intensively encoded originals show more relational retrieval (Novick 1988; Faries and Reiser 1988; Blanchette and Dunbar 2001), but this is cited secondhand.
agent_test: Test whether richer encoding at storage time (abstract summary) raises later structural retrieval.

claim: Memory written as distilled or abstracted entries beats retrieving raw past cases on agent benchmarks: AWM Mind2Web step SR 34.6 vs Synapse (retrieved examples) 30.6; ReasoningBank WebArena SR 48.8 vs Synapse 42.1 vs AWM 44.1 (no memory 40.5); Dynamic Cheatsheet curated memory beats raw retrieval in most rows and beats full-history appending (Sonnet AIME 2024 50.0 vs 26.7). Scope: task success, not a measured structural retrieval rate; gap 2 only partly closed.
agent_test: Write a short schema note (situation, mechanism, outcome) after each solved item; retrieve on notes vs on raw traces; log structural-match rate and task success.

claim: Putting more retrieved or stored material in the prompt does not scale: accuracy rises then falls with more passages (Long-context LLMs meet RAG), 20-30 documents can fall below closed-book 56.1 (Lost in the middle), full-history appending gave GPT-4o 6.7 vs baseline 20.0 on AIME 2024, and ReasoningBank success falls from 49.7 (1 item) to 44.4 (4 items). Hard negatives with the right surface and wrong structure are the likely cause.
agent_test: Inject at most 1-2 cases; order best first; compare against a stuffed-memory arm and a no-memory arm.

claim: Shortlist depth for an LLM reranker: on BRIGHT, GPT-4 reranking the top 10 vs top 100 gave 17.4 vs 17.0 (BM25 base 14.3) and 21.5 vs 22.6 (Google base 19.5). CPR's tournament used 151 candidates, cut to 40 then 10, and lost 8.3 percent of positives at the first cut. So 10-40 survivors is the working range; 10-20 percent of a thousand-item store (100-200) is not needed.
agent_test: On the agent's own store, vary the cheap-stage shortlist (10, 20, 40, 100) and measure rerank recall and tokens. Not yet tested on an agent-built store.

claim: Retrieve first and let the model flag 'cannot answer from this' before escalating: Self-Route reached long-context accuracy (GPT-4O 48.89 vs LC 48.67; Gemini 46.41 vs 49.70) at 61.4 and 38.4 percent of tokens. RAG and long-context predictions were identical for over 60 percent of queries.
agent_test: Escalate from 1-2 retrieved cases to more context only when the solver says the cases do not help. Knowledge QA evidence only.

claim: Gate retrieval instead of always retrieving: FLARE good at 40-80 percent of sentences and worse above 50-60 percent; PopQA adaptive retrieval retrieves for about 40 percent of questions with davinci-003 and rarely helps models under 10B; Self-RAG reports a large drop on PopQA and ASQA when it always retrieves the top passage (41.8 PopQA in that ablation; full-model row not recovered); HippoSpark gains turn unstable after about 5 calls and 10.67 percent of instances needed none. The threshold shifts with model strength.
agent_test: Trigger rule candidate: retrieve when the solver reports no clear next move, query with the current situation plus the local goal, cap at 3-5 calls, re-frame the state instead of retrieving again when the cap is hit. Tune the gate per model.

claim: Coverage caps the gain from retrieval: small stores give weak best matches (HippoSpark Biology 20 items, mean top-1 0.676 vs Chemistry 112 items, 0.751), and in CPR the analogy judgment discarded about 91 percent of cross-topic pairs. Combined with K23 (analogies about 3 percent of a corpus) an agent should expect no true analogue for most items.
agent_test: Log top-1 similarity and the verifier verdict on every query; report how often a true analogue exists before claiming retrieval gains.

claim: False analogies can be cut by independent narrow checks, but no study tests this on analogies. Chain-of-Verification raised list precision from 0.17 to 0.36 (two-step) and 0.32 (factored) with answers independent of the draft. CPR's two-call design (extract object mapping and relations, then check against a reject taxonomy: same problem, background only, unsupported mapping) agreed with a human at kappa 0.84 on 50 items.
agent_test: Before using a retrieved case, require an explicit role-by-role mapping and one independent check per mapped role; measure false-positive rate against token cost on a set with planted surface-match decoys.

claim: Gap 3 (compare two cases before retrieving, Gentner 2009 effect in an LLM): no study found. The only related item is ExpeL, which builds insights from failed-vs-successful trajectory pairs, but pair comparison is not ablated against single-trajectory abstraction.
agent_test: Give the agent two solved items to compare and write one shared principle, then retrieve with that principle; compare with retrieving on either item alone. Run on a small set with known structural twins.

claim: Gap 8 (familiar named structures raise structural retrieval in LLMs): untested. Indirect evidence is that LLM analogy accuracy falls with unfamiliar surface symbols (Greek and symbol alphabets, permuted alphabets) while people hold steady.
agent_test: Index cases with and without a named-pattern label (e.g. 'bottleneck', 'hidden invariant') and measure structural retrieval of twins with unusual surfaces.

claim: Gap 9 (crossover between self-generated analogues and retrieval): measured only on 2022-era models. Retrieval wins for curie-001 and davinci-001 and the two tie at davinci-002; self-generation wins by 4 points at davinci-003. Newer evidence points the same way but is indirect: the gain from self-generated exemplars on Codeforces falls from +2 to 0 from GPT-3.5 to GPT-4; CANA's gain over self-reflection falls from +0.67 (gpt-5.4-mini) to +0.06 (sonnet-4-6); DeepSeek-R1 reports few-shot prompting degrades it.
agent_test: For the current frontier model run three arms on the agent's own tasks: no help, self-generated analogues, retrieved cases from its own store. Expect self-generation to be enough unless the store holds knowledge the model lacks.
